entities.summary: Andrea dei Mozzi was an Italian bishop from the Mozzi family of bankers who served as papal chaplain to Pope Alexander IV and Pope Gregory IX. He was appointed Archbishop of Florence in 1287 and later became the Archbishop of Vicenza in 1295, but his appointment was controversial and led to a scandal that made him a character in Dante's The Inferno. As a result of his appointment, Andrea dei Mozzi played a significant role in the political and religious landscape of 14th-century Italy. His legacy as a prelate in the Catholic Church has endured, albeit with controversy, and continues to be studied by historians today.
